label: Inbound remittance: threshold for written confirmation of purpose
unit: USD equivalent, same day and same person
appliesTo: Receipts into Korea that do not otherwise require a foreign exchange declaration
why: Replaces the figure everyone repeats. Guidance in English almost universally states that inbound transfers above USD 10,000 are automatically reported and that USD 50,000 a year triggers a declaration; neither is the general rule for receiving money in Korea. What the regulations do set is a point at which the foreign exchange bank obtains written confirmation of why the money was received — an obligation on the bank, not a filing by the recipient, and a different thing from any declaration attaching to the underlying transaction.

history.source: Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulation — receipts not requiring declaration
history.note: Measured on the same day for the same person. Below it, ordinary receipts are broadly permitted without declaration. Where the underlying transaction is itself a capital transaction — overseas investment, a loan, acquisition of securities or real estate — the declaration requirements for that transaction apply regardless of amount, and are assessed first. Separately from all of this, a bank can request source-of-funds evidence under its anti-money-laundering and customer due diligence obligations, which is not a declaration.
